rationale: THE CLOSEST C++ CONSTRUCT TO `mixes_in`, MEASURED. The canonical contract (src/ast/types.ts, MixesIn) is 'a class COMPOSES a mixin into its supertype chain', measured on Dart's `class C with M`, where the `with` list is NOT an inheritance clause. C++ has exactly ONE construct for supertype composition — the base-clause — and EVERY entry in it declares a BASE CLASS (the is-a relation). That includes the CRTP idiom (`class Widget : public Mixin<Widget>`) and multi-base classes, which C++ programmers CALL mixins: the language still spells them as inheritance, so `extends` is the honest value. RULED on LANGUAGE semantics (there is no non-inheritance composition construct), and this fixture PINS that even the mixin-idiom base class emits `extends`, never `mixes_in`.
